messages.subject: Name for Gaussian observation component?
parts:
Hello, I am trying to generate posterior predictions at new points for an SPDE model using inlabru:

```
posterior_predictions <- generate(
  m_bru, 
  prediction_pixels, 
  ~ (1 + site))
```

Where m_bru is my model, prediction_pixels is a SpatialPointsDataFrame with the points I want to make predictions at, and site is the name of my SPDE component.

1. It seems that the result does not include samples of the nugget or what INLA calls "Gaussian observations". Is that right?

2. If so, how do I include random draws of the Gaussian observation noise in my simulations? Is there a name for that component I can add to the formula I pass to generate?

Thanks!
Eric

messages.author: 3ee56653c54cc755
messages.subject: Re: Name for Gaussian observation component?
parts:
~ data.frame(Precision_for_the_Gaussian_observations, 1 + site))
```
And then I would just manually generate the Gaussian noise using `rnorm(sd = sqrt(1/Precision_for_the_Gaussian_observations)`.

But I noticed something funny: the precisions seem to be reused quite frequently. For example, the first 15 samples in my case are exactly 119993.1, then the next 4 are exactly 151535.3. I don't see similar repetitions for `1 + site` samples. One workaround is to simply generate one sample at a time and then concatenate them but that is slow.

Is this a bug?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Name for Gaussian observation component?
parts:
Yes, see the more complete version in my other reply.

As for the discrete nature of the hyperparameters; yes, these posterior samples are generated by inla.posterior.sample, where the hyperparameters are only drawn from the points used in the numerical integration scheme over the hyperparameter distribution. There is currently no method for getting full samples of the hyperparameter samples jointly with the latent variables.

Finn
